and awaitingAssistantResponse = true as two separate synchronous

new $turnPhase subscription added in c2e29cf saw a transient .idle
emission (between the two writes, before .processing settles) and
fired .connected/"Mic ready" on every committed turn, reintroducing
the exact stomp this PR set out to fix.

commits.headline: fix(installer): match export-prefixed assignments in every .env writer
commits.body:
Switching the readers to dotenv widened what counts as a stale credential without
widening what the removers can delete. dotenv accepts `export AUTOMEM_API_KEY=...`;
the removers matched a bare `KEY=` only. So the reader correctly identified the key
as belonging to another endpoint, asked for its removal, and the line survived —
leaving the old credential live against the new host. That leak did not exist
before the dotenv migration; it was introduced by half-applying it.

commits.headline: fix(hermes): parse the provider .env with dotenv too
commits.body:
The previous commit switched install.ts and setup.ts to dotenv and claimed the
sweep was complete. A third hand-rolled reader was sitting in hermes-config.ts,
in a file this PR had already edited twice — so a provider .env written as
AUTOMEM_API_URL='https://x' or with a trailing comment compared as a different
endpoint, and a same-endpoint re-run deleted a working credential.

commits.headline: fix: refuse stray rules-file markers across all installer hosts
commits.body:
The "insert or replace a marked rules block" logic was copy-pasted into five
hosts. PR #197 hardened only the Grok copy: a file holding two start markers and
one end contains both markers, so an indexOf-based check calls it well-formed and
replaces from the first start through the end — silently deleting the second
marker and whatever the user wrote between them.

commits.headline: fix(installer): parse .env with dotenv instead of hand-rolled readers
commits.body:
Both readers that the credential pairing depends on disagreed with the parser
that actually loads these files at server startup. install.ts unwrapped only
double quotes and never stripped comments; setup.ts did the same. So a project
.env written as AUTOMEM_API_URL='https://x' or with a trailing # comment compared
as a different endpoint, and a re-run at the *same* endpoint removed a
still-valid key and left the project unauthenticated.

commits.headline: fix(openclaw): shadow rejected skill credentials instead of deleting them
commits.body:
The previous commit established that rejection has to be written as a blank
rather than omitted, because a host layers the entry env over its own. It applied
that to the Grok and Hermes entries and left OpenClaw's skill entry deleting both
names — two of three hosts, which is the same incompleteness this PR exists to
fix, one commit after stating the rule.

commits.headline: fix(uitests): seed a real plan task for UITEST_SEED_PLAN_APPROVAL
commits.body:
Codex P1, and correct. The hook reused the agent-visibility approval fixture,
whose attentionType is "permission". StructuredResponseCard.kind(forAttentionType:)
routes that through AttentionKind to .permission — a card whose controls are
permissioncard.*, not plancard.* — so testPlanCardIdentifiersResolve could never
have passed against this seed. The hook's own doc comment promised the opposite.

commits.headline: fix(installer): shadow rejected credentials at the process boundary
commits.body:
Omitting a rejected key from a server entry does not stop it reaching the server.
The host launches the child with the entry's env layered over its own
(`{...process.env, ...entry.env}`), so a shell-exported AUTOMEM_API_KEY — issued
for whatever endpoint that shell names — is inherited by a child whose URL the
entry just pointed somewhere else. Rejection has to be written, not merely
omitted.

credential genuinely issued for A, so it accepted the pair and wrote B's token

when it inherited its environment from the host: Grok setup then refused to
update it, uninstall skipped it, and Hermes migration could leave the legacy
`memory` registration beside the new `automem

commits.headline: ci: gate PRs on the Mac Catalyst build
commits.body:
The Xcode Cloud "Desktop" workflow archives macOS and ships it to TestFlight
internal, and it was just narrowed from any-branch to main-only. That leaves no
pre-merge check on Catalyst: a Catalyst-only break would land on main, fail that
archive, and silently produce no new Mac TestFlight build — found whenever
someone next went to test the desktop app.

commits.headline: fix(local): lead the merged MLX message with the boundary
commits.body:
History can end with a user turn that is not this turn — a racing injection, or
the previous turn when this one's assistant reply never persisted. The MLX
dedupe deliberately leaves it (the content does not match), and
normalizeHistoryMessages then coalesces it with the appended current turn into
a single message.

commits.headline: fix(local): give local model turns the resumed-conversation boundary
commits.body:
Part of #1267. #1266 moved the boundary to `buildClaudeRequestMessages`, the
one place every *cloud* surface's current turn passes through. LocalModelService
defines its own `streamMessageCanonical` and never reaches it, so a local turn
was the one surface that could not tell three weeks had passed — the same shape
as #1248, where local models had no date anchor for exactly this reason.

commits.headline: fix(agents): date a synthesized completion so it can be judged stale
commits.body:
The terminal write `reconcileMissingSessions` synthesizes is ordered against
the row's stored activity by its `lastSeenAt` — and it could have none. Two
independent sources of that timestamp can be absent at once:
`normalizeClaudeCodeAgentSession` derives it from `startedAt`, which is
`undefined` when the agents_json entry has no parseable one, and the transcript
pass overrides it only when a transcript actually resolves.

commits.headline: fix(agents): retry the completion write instead of failing the task
commits.body:
Round-4 Codex P1 on #1274. Throwing on an unpersistable completion reached
the execution retry loop, where `task_completion_persist_failed` matches no
retryable pattern — so `_handleTaskFailure()` marked a task that genuinely
succeeded as failed, notified the user, and discarded the result. Surfacing
the failure was right; routing it through execution failure was not.

commits.headline: fix(agents): tell a persistence failure apart from a lost CAS
commits.body:
Round-2 Codex P1 on #1274. `completeTask()` returns false for a lost CAS and
also for a transient Prisma error, a missing row, or a refused completion.
Treating every false as "recovery won" meant a DB hiccup silently discarded a
finished task: the executor released its lane, finalization and the completion
event were suppressed, and the durable row stayed `running` with nobody told.

commits.headline: fix(agents): make the completion write a compare-and-set too
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1274. The recovery CAS only rejected completion writes that
landed BEFORE it. A normal in-process completion finishing just after the
claim called an unconditional `agentRun.update()`, leaving durable state
`completed` while the reaper had already emitted task_review and set the
cached task to `awaiting_review`.

commits.headline: fix(agents): fence normal completion in stale-recovery CAS
commits.body:
The stale-recovery path in _reapStaleTasks could overwrite a task that
had already completed normally: it patched recovery context into the
DB unconditionally, then CAS'd only on expectedStatus (no version
check), so a concurrent normal-completion transition could still lose
to a stale reaper claiming awaiting_review after the fact.

commits.headline: fix(install): keep an inherited API key paired with its endpoint
commits.body:
The guided installer read AUTOMEM_API_KEY from the environment and passed it to
the per-host installers as an *explicit* apiKey — which is the highest-precedence
input, so it bypassed the endpoint-pairing check applyGrokSetup had just gained.
`install --endpoint https://new.example` with the old host's key exported
therefore persisted that credential for the new host.

fix(grok): close the seam when removing a mid-file AutoMem table
commits.body:
The fidelity tests all ended up with [mcp_servers.memory] at end-of-file, where
trailing-newline normalization hid a real bug: when the table sits between two
others, removing it leaves the blank line before it adjacent to the one after it.
TOML ignores the extra blank, so the splice verification accepted it and every
install/uninstall cycle added another line.

commits.body:

commits.headline: feat(history): mark conversations resumed after a long silence
commits.body:
Sessions here are long-lived by design — a Telegram chat or Slack DM keeps one
session id forever, so telegram--5178868641 spans 21 days / 174 messages. But
replayed history carried no timing at all, so a message sent eight days after
the previous one looked exactly like the next sentence of a continuous
exchange, and the model answered as if nothing had happened in between.

commits.headline: fix(memory): keep the recency guidance out of the token-budgeted serializer
commits.body:
Codex P1 (3771154382). MEMORY_RECENCY_GUIDANCE is a fixed ~300 characters and
was appended to serializeMemoriesToText's header after every totalChars/charLimit
check, so it never counted toward tokenBudget. memory-cache.js calls that

commits.headline: fix(memory): stamp rewritten memories with their rewrite date
commits.body:
Codex P1 (3770869167). update_memory rewrites a memory's content in place while
keeping its original creation date, but getMemoryTimestampMs only ever read the
creation fields. A memory rewritten today was therefore stamped weeks ago, and
MEMORY_RECENCY_GUIDANCE then instructed the model to resolve the NEW content's
"tomorrow" against the OLD day — reproducing the exact temporal-grounding
failure these stamps exist to prevent.

commits.headline: fix(memory): stamp recalled memories with the date they were written
commits.body:
A recalled memory is a record of something that was true when it was written,
but every live renderer emitted content only. With no age signal, absolute dates
inside a memory read as current: on 2026-08-11 a voice turn recalled a trip
itinerary stored before departure and narrated it as "drive up to Hamilton today
(Aug 1)" — after the trip had already ended. The current date WAS in that system
prompt; what was missing was how old the memory was.

commits.headline: fix(mcp-sse): emit the stored date in compact recall output
commits.body:
The default (non-detailed) recall block rendered content, tags, score and ID
but dropped the memory's stored timestamp. A caller replaying that text had no
way to tell a note written today from one written six weeks ago, so absolute
dates inside the content read as if they were current — an agent recalling a
trip itinerary written before departure narrated it in the present tense ten
days after the trip ended.

commits.headline: fix(cli): re-rank corrected candidates, enforce the candidate cap per node
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The aria-hidden correction pass now ranks the
corrected set from scratch instead of taking the first positive corrected score,
so a candidate that becomes an exact match after correction is not beaten by an
earlier prefix match. The 4000-node candidate cap is checked per node and before
each shadow-root descent rather than only on entry, and dedupe uses a Set, so a
single large root can no longer push an unbounded set through the per-node
layout and hit-test work.

commits.headline: fix(cli): walk the full ranked set, and never re-send a delivered release
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. pickClickCandidate returns `ranked` (the full ordered
set) so the aria-hidden correction pass is not capped at the three-item
runnersUp slice, which made a genuine candidate unreachable behind decoys
matching only on hidden text. The pointer sequence records which events it
delivered, so interruption cleanup cannot send a second mouseup and run
document-level release handlers twice.

commits.headline: fix(cli): confine the label-read mutation, cancel interrupted pointers, recheck disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. Scoring uses plain innerText and writes nothing; only
the ranked winner is re-read with aria-hidden descendants hidden, falling through
to the next candidate if that correction kills the match. An interrupted pointer
sequence now dispatches pointercancel and mouseup on a still-connected target so
document-level pressed/drag state is not left stuck. Disabledness is rechecked
before the click event, since a mousedown handler can disable the control
mid-sequence.

commits.headline: fix(cli): exclude aria-hidden by hiding and re-reading; stop a click mid-sequence
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. aria-hidden content is excluded by setting
display:none on the outermost aria-hidden descendants, reading innerText, and
restoring the previous inline value — string subtraction could not tell which
occurrence of repeated text came from the hidden node, and was wrong in both DOM
orderings. The pointer sequence now checks isConnected between events and stops
if a handler removed the control, reporting which event it stopped before rather
than dispatching the rest at a d

commits.headline: fix(cli): score before visibility, keep disabled exact matches, use :disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The comparator now orders exact > prefix > substring
before visibility, so a visible partial match cannot outrank a hidden exact one
and dispatch a broader action. Disabled candidates are scored with the rest of
the pool and checked on the winner, so a disabled exact match is reported as
disabled rather than replaced by an enabled prefix match. Disabledness uses
matches(':disabled') plus aria-disabled instead of a fieldset[disabled] ancestor
scan, which was refusing li

commits.headline: fix: declare the disjoint Node range pdf-parse actually supports (#71)
commits.body:
package.json claimed `>=20.16.0`, but pdf-parse@2.4.5 declares
`>=20.16.0 <21 || >=22.3.0` — a disjoint range. We were therefore
claiming support for Node 21.x and 22.0-22.2, where an engine-strict
install fails or PDF extraction is unavailable. The README's "20.16.0 or
newer" repeated the same overclaim, and that README ships inside the
published tarball.

commits.headline: fix(cli): disabled controls, occluded ranking, repeated aria-hidden text
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. Disabled controls (disabled property, aria-disabled,
disabled ancestor fieldset) are excluded from candidates and rejected on the
selector path — dispatchEvent does not honour native disabled suppression, so
automation could otherwise fire a disabled destructive action. Visibility now
hit-tests at the candidate box centre so an overlay-covered control cannot win
visible-first ranking over its live duplicate. The aria-hidden subtraction
removes one occurrence per outerm

Syncs cli-js with autohub. Full reasoning in that commit; the short version is

visible, an untrusted pointer sequence opens Google Maps' Directions panel
(reproduced twice). Maps accepts untrusted events, so trusted dispatch bought
nothing while the resolve/dispatch split cost a new defect per review round.

commits.body:
Plain coalescing of tools/list_changed left the hub serving stale schemas
indefinitely. A tools/list response describing state A and a later
notification announcing state B can arrive in the same stdout chunk;
handleServerOutput parses that chunk synchronously, so B joined A's

two-notifications-in-one-chunk probe: one tools/list call, tools stuck at A.
A dirty flag now forces exactly one trailing fetch, so a burst costs two
round

commits.headline: fix(mcp): close the three P1 gaps Codex found on the lifecycle PR
commits.body:
closeRemoteServer never reached client.close()/transport.close() when
terminateSession() threw synchronously: Promise.allSettled evaluates its
argument array before it is called, so the throw escaped the whole helper.
Shutdown then cleared the maps with a live HTTP client and session behind
them — a leak on every such shutdown. Both allSettled sites now capture a
synchronous throw as a rejection.

commits.headline: fix(frontier): never certify queue health from the dry-run subset
commits.body:
Codex P1 round 2: `--dry-run` leaves the cycle's candidateDbPath null, so the
health report fell back to `topCandidates` — priority-sorted and `--limit`
capped — and an aged persisted candidate absent from that subset produced
`status: "healthy"`. Same false-healthy shape as the 200-row window, one
branch over.

commits.headline: fix(frontier): scan every tracked candidate for the SLA check
commits.body:
Codex P1: `listCandidates` clamps to 200 rows per status, sorts by priority,
and offers no offset — so past 200 tracked rows the SLA scan silently dropped
exactly the aged low-priority candidate it exists to find, and the report
claimed "healthy" on a queue it had not fully read. That is the same
aggregate-hides-the-individual failure #1025 is about, one level up.

commits.headline: fix: make soft stdin EOF a true no-op
commits.body:

SDK onclose and breaks one-shot pipe flows. Hard exit only on parent
watchdog reparent and SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP. Capture parentPid before
any await; unit tests assert stdin EOF alone does not exit.

the event loop drain; parent-watchdog + signals still hard-exit orphans.

commits.headline: fix: soft-close stdin EOF so one-shot pipe calls can finish
commits.body:
Hard process.exit on stdin end/close raced the documented
`echo … | npm start` tool probe (AGENTS.md) and could kill in-flight
handlers before the MCP response was written. Close the transport on EOF
and let the event loop drain; parent-watchdog + signals still hard-exit
orphans that keep stdin open.

commits.headline: fix(voice): await prior interrupt teardown in dispose() via pendingPlayerTeardown
commits.body:
killPlayer() nulls the shared player reference synchronously while the
underlying process exits asynchronously. When shutdown follows shortly after
a barge-in interrupt(), dispose() saw player === null and resolved early
instead of awaiting the in-flight teardown, racing the unref'd SIGKILL
backstop.

commits.body:
throwCruiseSpeed 0.08, settled on device, and it took three passes because I had

nothing travels slower than it, so a gentle toss is accelerated UP to it. At 0.5
every throw felt forceful -- "if I just give it a gentle toss it goes a bit faster
than I would expect" -- and at the original 0.075 a throw died in five feet. 0.08
keeps a gentle toss gentle; the six-second half-life is what carries a hard one.
Half-life own

commits.body:
_FieldExpansion and _InflowRate are amplitude dials that BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels
republishes as tuning constants every frame, so folding them straight into
radialScale produced a fixed offset rather than a breath -- the Field | Inflow role
existed specifically to make the room expand and contract with the pulse, and it
never did. _BeatEnergy is the one channel that actually varies with the beat, so it
now gates how much of the dialed range applies each frame, the same
envelope-times-amplitude

commits.headline: fix(starfield): size mesh bounds to the dials' actual permitted expansion
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.Create padded bounds by a flat 25% over the baked
volume, but TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert can scale a star's radial
distance by up to 2x (radialScale = 1 + _FieldExpansion - _InflowRate,
each clamped to [0, 1] by BlackHoleVisualTuning). fieldExpansion ships at
1.0 today, so a low inflowRate during a tuning sweep could pop stars out
of the frustum edge -- Unity culls against these baked bounds, not the
vertex shader's runtime result.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): pick the volume's actual longest axis for the sampling fallback
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.SampleHome's exhausted-rejection-sampling fallback
always placed its point on Z at the volume's longest half-extent, even
when X or Y was the longer axis. An 8x4x2 volume's longest axis is X, so
the fallback returned (0, 0, 4) -- 4m out on a Z axis whose half-extent is
only 1m, outside both the volume and the mesh bounds.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): enforce the min pull distance on a star's final position
commits.body:
_MinPullDistance only ever floored the pull-strength denominator in
TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert; the destination lerp toward the singularity
was unbounded, so a close pass could still carry a star to within ~4% of
the singularity despite the dial. The comfort guarantee it advertises --
no star ever yanked through the wearer's face -- was false as written.

commits.headline: fix(canary): honor ENV_PATH; never discard grant-smoke evidence
commits.body:
Codex P1 (agent-kernel-e2e.js): readRuntimeAuthEnv defaulted to <repo>/.env
even when the launcher set ENV_PATH, so a canary pointed at a non-default
environment file silently used a stale default key — or none — while the
configured credential went unused. It now resolves baseEnv.ENV_PATH first,
matching load-env.js and every other script here. This reads the launching

objection stands, so the ring is capped at _RoomRingRadius in the vertex
shader (fill-rate budget, not fragment) and dissolves before it reaches
the wearer, and is gated on _SingularityWS.w the same way the pull is, so

DefaultPullStrength (1f) and DefaultInfallRate (0.35f) are already non-zero, so
the moment a future task wires those dials to the shader, a disabled writer would
leave every star pulling toward a black hole that is no longer there.

commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.calmTarget was scaled by PulseAmplitude alone,
which ramps toward 1 on measurement freshness regardless of contact
state. A contact-capable strap that keeps streaming NotDetected after
it comes off therefore kept being treated as genuine calmness, holding

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): verify arrival distance before raising SummonArrived
commits.body:
TrialGPhysicsController ends a recall (EndRecallDrive) purely because
its fixed-duration curve elapsed, whether or not the body actually
reached the target -- a room collider blocking the dynamic body ends
the drive the exact same way as a clean delivery. TrialGSummonController
read IsRecalling == false alone as "arrived" and raised SummonArrived
unconditionally, so a recall blocked behind a wall could still announce
arrival while the black hole stayed far outside ArrivalDistance.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the summon flash a signal-independent gain
commits.body:
The summon gesture works with no heart-rate source connected, but its
body flash was multiplied by `warm` (_WarmColor * _WarmAmount), and
_WarmAmount is 0 by default until a live rate produces calmness. In a
release session where BLE has not connected -- the default state for
any wearer without a strap -- the hand rings would announce a summon
arrival while the black hole itself answered with nothing.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): reject non-finite values in the UDP tuning protocol
commits.body:
float.TryParse accepts "NaN" and "Infinity" as well-formed numbers, and
neither Mathf.Clamp nor Mathf.Clamp01 sanitizes them -- both of Clamp's
comparisons are false for NaN, so it passes straight through. A message
like "beatsizeamount=NaN" over UDP could therefore reach
BlackHoleVisualTuning.BeatSizeAmount, which now feeds directly into
pulseTarget.localScale (BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.LateUpdate), poisoning
the black hole's transform.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): gate published beat energy on trustworthy signal
commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels published _BeatEnergy unconditionally even
when BlackHoleBeatTreatmentMath.HasTrustworthySignal was false (e.g. a
contact-capable strap reporting NotDetected). PulseAmplitude ramps up
from measurement freshness alone, so the envelope stayed nonzero and
TrialAEmissive/TrialAParticles kept brightening and expanding the body
after the strap was removed, contradicting the "strap removed -> warm
response goes to nothing" acceptance criterion.

commits.body:
The spec asks for continuous weights so crossing a treatment boundary
does not pop. TreatmentBlendHalfLife existed as a pinned constant with
nothing reading it — BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels assigned
ResolveWeights' output to _weights directly, so crossing the 1.5 m
distance band was a one-frame cut from (size 1.0, ember 0.7) to
(shockwave 1.0). The half-life's own contract test asserted only the
constant's value, which would pass against this no-op.

commits.body:
The tuning page showed MIX/BAND/FORCED/FIELD/INFLOW/WARM/BEAT/LAST but
omitted emberAmount and shockwaveAmount — the one dial the plan
explicitly leaves unsettled pending the user's on-device re-judgement.
During that session the wearer would turn the shockwave dial and get no
on-screen confirmation it landed, only the LAST line's raw echo of the
last accepted message, which is one message stale.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): wire BeatSizeAmount into the pulse's size treatment
commits.body:
BeatSizeAmount was advertised by tune-udp.py, parsed and clamped by
BlackHoleVisualTuning.TryApply, reset by ResetToDefaults, pinned by a
test and displayed live on the tuning HUD as "BEAT: 0.06" — but nothing
consumed it. A dial that reports success and does nothing is worse than
an absent one: a developer sends beatSizeAmount=0.3, watches the HUD
confirm it, and sees no change.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the warm gate a floor the tuning rig can reach
commits.body:
_WarmAmount gated every warm treatment (ember, shockwave ring, breath
bloom, summon flash) as calmness * WarmAmount. Calmness is exactly 0 at
90+ BPM and ~0.39 at a normal standing 75 BPM, so at an elevated heart
rate treatment selection had no visible effect at all — and because
WarmAmount was a multiplier, sending warmAmount=1 over UDP could not
force it back on. The tuning rig structurally could not reach the
failure it exists to let a developer diagnose.

commits.body:

clearing it first, unlike Redraw()'s page-0 path. DrawText/DrawGlyph only

commits.body:
The recall's only feedback is the lasso's rope, borrowed. Both of its
preconditions fail silently: a null line array or an unresolved target
collider skips the draw and returns, so the hole would still fly back
with nothing to show the gesture had fired. Neither is visible from the
summon's own logic, and the existing composition test stopped at "the
three components resolved" — which a silently inert indicator passes.

commits.headline: feat(trial-g): zip the summon back on an eased sub-second curve
commits.body:
The recall drove through the lasso's Selected path, which is deliberately
gentle — 0.55 m/s, eased in over 0.3 s — because it is a manipulation. A
room crossing at that speed took about five seconds, which is why the
timeout was six. A recall is a restart, not a manipulation, so it gets its
own drive: a fixed 0.6 s flight regardless of distance, so the gesture
reads the same whether the hole is across the room or just out of reach.

and "no thank you" (0.75) all cleared 0.6, so genuine replies that merely

commits.headline: fix(voice): suppress noisy echoes of short assistant replies
commits.body:
The reverse-containment check required the assistant's reply to be at
least 12 characters, and the run-coverage check below it requires a
20-character shared run. A short reply echoed back with STT noise on the
front cleared neither: "Sounds good" (11 chars) coming back as "Uh,
sounds good" failed exact equality, skipped the containment branch on
length, and produced an 11-char run under the 20-char floor. The echo
read as a genuine turn and the agent could answer its own voice.

subscribes rather than when a beat arrives. CanTakeRigFrom gated on
state alone, so a dry strap locked the LAN bridge out permanently.
That is exactly the hardware-free test loop the bridge exists to
provide, defeated by a sensor nobody was wearing.

commits.body:
Keep Silero reset/endSegment serialized with in-flight ONNX work by
enqueueing reset after the existing packet tail instead of replacing it.
Treat Chatterbox model_loaded:false as retryable during startup polling.

commits.headline: fix(agents): route task control from managed sites
fix(autojack): close seven Codex P1 fail-opens on the human-risk gate
commits.body:
Round 6 on #1040. Tighten the reset --hard doc carve-out so an unrelated
Document verb cannot exempt a later wipe; let buy/purchase take ordinary
nouns while scoping that rule (and sync/rename production-data) to
question/options/context so task titles cannot fold in; drop the mandatory
digit on opaque credential literals; page run/do/start the deploy; cover
synchronize/synchronise; and gate SSN/PHI privacy vocabulary.

commits.headline: feat(tui): restore panel zoom on m
commits.body:
Panel zoom was silently dropped in the conversation-first redesign (#45) and
never restored. `m` now collapses the desktop split so the focused destination
owns the whole body, following focus across tab switches.

commits.headline: fix(push): send the gateway credential to protected registry routes
commits.body:
899e853 put `requireAuth` in front of `POST /v1/device-tokens` and the new
`POST /v1/activity-tokens`. The gateway checks those against
PUSH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, but the app only ever sent the hub `apiKey` and no
gateway credential existed anywhere in Settings or UserDefaults. A gateway
deployed with its own secret therefore answered 401 to both device and Live
Activity registration, silently dropping push delivery.

commits.headline: test(slack): pin cleanMessage bot ID without env coupling
commits.body:
Local/dev checkouts resolve workspace bot identity (or an unresolved
placeholder) instead of SLACK_BOT_USER_ID, so the alias-normalization
assertion was environment-dependent.

commits.headline: fix(voice): serialize Silero VAD control ops with packet queue
commits.body:
Queue endSegment/reset behind the audio FIFO and invalidate pending
packets on reset so commit/clear cannot race queued ONNX processing.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): grow the black hole as the heart rate slows, and wire the LAN bridge
commits.body:
Slower heart, bigger black hole — the mapping the throb was built to carry.
As the smoothed rate falls from 90 to 55 bpm the Trial G art root grows
smoothly to 1.6x, easing on a 7-second half-life so it reads as breathing
rather than as twitching on ordinary respiratory variation. It multiplies
with the beat envelope, so a slow heart is a large black hole that is still
visibly beating. Neither multiplier touches the black hole's diameter, which
also sizes the SphereCollider used to grab it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): address Codex P1s on echo suppression
commits.body:
- Re-arm auto-sleep after suppressing an echo. speech-start and speech-stop
  both cancelScheduledSleep(), so the suppression branch was the only terminal
  path in processFinalTranscript leaving no timer armed — mic stayed hot
  indefinitely. The prior comment's premise was wrong: scheduleSleep() is the
  ordinary 45s idle timer, not forceSleep().

commits.headline: fix(slack): keep bot-ID detection working when the base class passes a message
commits.body:
PlatformAdapter.handleIncomingMessage now forwards the normalized message in
the positional slot SlackAdapter.detectMention treats as an explicit bot-ID
override, so its regex was built from "[object Object]" and aliased mention
tokens like <@U09CWNC42KE|auto_jack> stopped matching. Only a string is
treated as an override now.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): gate the passive voice, and stop doc wording from exempting execution
commits.body:
Codex round 5 on #1040. Four of the five findings are the same shape: a
rule enumerated the ACTIVE voice and English asked in the passive.

commits.headline: test(api): exercise the successful iOS task-response route
commits.body:
The route test only covered schema rejection, so the iOS routing
regression it was meant to guard could have returned unnoticed. Drive a
valid iOS response through the real router, bridge, and Prisma store on
a pushed throwaway schema, and assert the waiting task reaches the queue
resume instead of the bridge's interaction_request_not_found.

commits.headline: fix(sync): prune task cache to empty only on authoritative total==0
commits.body:
An empty `/v1/tasks` response could reconcile the local Task cache to empty
and wipe it. A degraded hub returning `200 {"tasks": []}` while its task
store is unavailable decodes to an authoritative-looking empty array, so
pruning on it caused the exact data loss this branch guards against.

commits.headline: fix(sync): reapply lifecycle/attention on stale task payloads
commits.body:
899e853 dropped the `applyLifecycleAndAttention` call from `mergeTask`'s
stale-payload branch (the early return taken when the remote `updatedAt` is
not newer than the local one). That branch is exactly how a terminal status
arriving on an older-stamped payload clears a stranded `needs_input`
attention, so tasks could stay parked in "needs you" forever after they
finished.

commits.headline: fix(api): forward terminal SSE sweeps to status-filtered clients
commits.body:
The reaper flips a task to interrupted/cancelled before emitting
task_stale/task_expired, so gating those events on the status filter
dropped the exact transition a status-filtered client needs to clear its
card. Match terminal sweeps on identity/platform only.

commits.headline: feat(tui): shift-jumps + directional expand/collapse
commits.body:
Add shift+up / shift+down as jump-to-top / jump-to-bottom alongside g/G,
and right/l = expand-only, left/h = collapse-only beside the existing
space toggle.

commits.headline: fix(voice): gate Chatterbox health on model_loaded; restore split-dropped config
commits.body: Address Codex P1 findings on #1032:

commits.headline: fix(whatsapp): fail closed when legacy reply identities are absent
commits.body:
An older bridge that omits both quotedIsFromMe and quotedSender left the
legacy fallback comparing two empty normalizations, so any quoted message
with an AutoJack-looking prefix counted as a verified bot reply. Require
both identities to be known before trusting that fallback.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close two fail-open gate holes; bind prod scope to its noun
commits.body:
Codex round 4 on #1040. Two of the four findings were fail-open — the
direction this PR exists to close — and both came from the same mistake:
gating on an ALLOWLIST of phrasings, where anything unlisted escapes.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): bind buy/order/reset --hard to an object or an intent
commits.body:
Codex round 3 on #1040 filed four P1s, all the same false-positive shape as
round 2: a bare word folded in from a task title and paged every question
asked under that task. Three were introduced by this PR and are fixed here;
each was reproduced against merged main first to confirm it was a regression
and not the standing behaviour.

commits.headline: docs(verification): record dev Slack smoke
fix(agents): harden Cloudflare operator boundaries
ci: support merge queue checks
feat(heart-rate): scan for an unpaired strap, and scope the docs to evidence
commits.body:
Until now the BLE bridge could only reach a strap this headset had already
bonded with, which made the transport useless on anyone else's device. It now
walks the bonded devices first (last-known-good address first, so the common
case stays fast) and falls back to an active BLE scan when none of them
exposes 0x180D. The scan is rate-guarded, runs in a 10 s window, and accepts a
device either on a 0x180D service-UUID advertisement or, as a second chance, on
a name that looks like a strap -- some

commits.headline: fix(bridge): forward native WhatsApp activation metadata (#173)
fix(autojack): scope the new gate rules to their target (Codex round 2)
commits.body:
Four P1 findings on the first cut of #1036, all the same defect in two
directions: a rule keyed off words appearing ANYWHERE in the text that
routingText() folds together, rather than off the thing being acted on.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close 13 verified fail-open holes in the judge's human-risk gate
commits.body:
classifyQuestionRoute() auto-answers unless a denylist regex matches, so every
phrasing the list misses becomes an autonomous action by an already-authorized
worker — there is no second gate downstream. With JUDGE_MODE=live and
JUDGE_PROMOTE_ALL=true (the active local config), 15 of 17 Codex-named probes
reached the judge on merged main.

commits.headline: fix(voice): name the source of a bad smoke scenario and refresh the env sample
commits.body:
Codex P1: .env.example documented VOICE_CONVERSATION_SMOKE_SCENARIO=basic, a
value that was never a real scenario, so anyone who copied it would now hit
the fail-closed guard on every run. Replace the stale sample with the valid
names plus a migration note, and name the offending source in the error so an
operator who never typed --scenario knows it came from .env or their shell.

commits.headline: fix(voice): fail closed on an unknown conversation-smoke scenario name
commits.body:
An explicitly requested scenario that is not a builtin used to fall back to
the 4-turn default suite and could report pass, so the harness read as "the
scenario I asked for passed" when a different scenario ran. Distinguish an
explicit request from the implicit default and throw on an unknown explicit
name, listing the valid scenarios. Scenario files still win over an inherited
stale scenario name so voice-eval runs are unaffected.

commits.headline: fix(cloudflare): enforce canonical deployment grants
feat(tui): swap space and x — quick-view vs interrupt
commits.body:
Space now expands the selected row (quick-view) and x interrupts the
assistant, matching how operators reach for the two actions: expand is
the high-frequency browsing verb, interrupt is the deliberate one.

Bring back the parked mcp-tools registry refresh, college-bros agent
names, wake-word model binaries, and gitignore entries for wyoming /

fix(tui): mouse gate + wheel-by-column
commits.body:
The overlay pointer gate listed help and the palette but not the
fresh-conversation confirm, so a wheel under that overlay moved a cursor
the operator could not see. The gate now matches workspaceBody's

commits.headline: docs(heart-rate): scope BLE status claims to the evidence that backs them
commits.body:
The permission-dialog row said verified on the strength of a focused
GrantPermissionsActivity, which does not identify which permission it
belongs to. Closed by elimination instead: every other runtime permission
reads granted=true after the reinstall and only the two Bluetooth ones read
false, so no other permission is left for that dialog to be. The reasoning
is now in the row rather than the conclusion alone.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): direct BLE bridge, permission wait, and provenance HUD
commits.body:
Lands the Java half of the direct-BLE transport, fixes a race that would have
made the first launch after install fail every time, and adds an in-headset
readout that says where the heartbeat came from.

commits.headline: fix(agents): bind escalations to task attempts
Fix iOS task response routing
fix(tui): transcript follow — tab-switch reset, coverage, pending pill
commits.body:
Scrollback is a reading position inside the transcript view, so leaving that
view ends the read. Every destination transition now routes through
activateWorkspaceTab and re-engages follow (offset→0): explicit 1-5, tab
cycling, the diagnostics shortcut, and the esc-return branch, which previously
set ActiveTab by hand. From a sidecar tab no key or wheel can reach the
transcript offset, so a stale offset stranded the transcript above the live
tail for the rest of the session — Jack's reported bug.

Skip writes after client close, and resolve ledger/queue tasks before
applying filters so filtered SSE clients only see matching events.

commits.headline: feat(voice): offline profile refresh and STT/VAD/TTS reliability
commits.body:
Switch offline defaults to dana_escalating / Fred Rezone, add Parakeet

Chatterbox health/stream recovery plus the persona-voice shim.

commits.body:
Use bridge-provided quotedIsFromMe and mentionedJIDs so group replies and

Full working-tree snapshot before splitting into WhatsApp, voice, and

commits.headline: index on main: 00a23724 fix(agents): dispatch e2e + harden runner health for voice (#1024)
fix(live): reopen attention when task re-enters needs-input
commits.body:
When a task_changed (or legacy agent_task) event moves a task back into a
needsInput-normalized status after a prior prompt was resolved, the merge
handlers only updated task.status and left the stale attentionResolvedAt set.
Task.requiresUserAttention rejects any task with a non-nil resolved marker, so
the re-opened prompt never resurfaced. Mirror the mergeTaskStatusUpdate path:
on a needsInput transition, reset attentionResolvedAt and establish the
fallback attentionType. Applies the same fix

commits.headline: fix(web): authorize capability approvals
fix(tui): transcript line index + span/window reconciliation
commits.body:
Block spans and rendered transcript lines were derived by two separate
walks. The render walk inserts a blank spacer row before each new speaker
turn and appends the live/draft tail; the span walk did neither, so every
reported span drifted one row per preceding speaker turn and reveal
targeting, the sticky header, and (soon) click hit-testing all resolved to
the wrong rows.

fix(autojack): restore merge/push to the human gate as ship-action
commits.body:
AGENTS.md names "deploys/merges/pushes" Red tier. The 2026-07-21 narrowing
dropped all three as "routine self-scoped dev vocabulary" and the replay
harness went further, asserting that "merge this branch into main and push?"
must NOT page. That assertion contradicted the repo's own rule, and I had

fix(autojack): close four routing gaps and redact the judge log
commits.body:
Codex round-2 P1s on the narrowed human-risk gate. Each was a question that
reached the live autojudge but should have paged Jack.

fix(live): clear attention on terminal live tasks; preserve remote updatedAt
commits.body: Addresses two Codex P2 findings on the live-updates merge path:

commits.headline: fix(autojack): gate judge promotion on the active model's own rows
commits.body:
Codex P1: `promote` was computed from the whole calibration window, so a
window spanning the Opus->Sonnet flip could put the new judge live on a
record it never earned. 19 correct Opus rows plus 1 incorrect Sonnet row
reads as 95% over 20 samples and promotes Sonnet on an 0/1 record of its
own. `mixedModel` was only informational, and no operator is in the
JudgePromotionController.refresh() -> getMode() -> auto-answer path, so an
operator-visible warning could not guard it.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close gate holes from narrowing + fix replay dedup
commits.body:
Codex P1s on the narrowed HUMAN_RISK_PATTERNS. Narrowing the gate to stop
paging on routine dev vocabulary also opened three holes that are not policy
changes — each one is a documented Red-tier invariant (AGENTS.md) and is on the
judge profile's own escalate list ("money movement, secret exposure, destroying
data, or contacting real third parties"). #1028 also force-promotes to live
auto-answering, so these are reachable without Jack, not theoretical.

commits.headline: test(voice): run local-voice-controller suite in test:voice
commits.body:
test/local-voice-controller.test.js was an orphan — referenced by no npm
script, so its 12 cases (including the sleep-timer invariant the echo
suppressor now depends on) never ran in CI. Wire it into test:voice.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): stop persisting gated question text; gate datastore resets
commits.body: Codex P1 #1 and #5 on this PR.

commits.headline: test(voice): guard sleep-timer invariant the echo suppressor relies on
commits.body:
The assistant-echo suppression path no longer calls scheduleSleep() when it
discards a transcript — doing so ended the session outright whenever the
classification was wrong. That is only safe because the sleep timer armed when
the assistant finished speaking survives interrupt() and still fires.

commits.headline: fix(runtime): resolve Codex P2 findings on task/watch paths
commits.body:
- removeTasks: decode TaskLifecycleEventPayload with the flexible
  hub-date strategy (matching mergeSnapshot/mergeSingleTask/
  mergeTaskChanged) so lifecycle removal events carrying ISO-8601
  dates no longer throw and get silently dropped.
- push-gateway: gitignore the runtime-written activity-tokens.json
  (APNs Live Activity tokens), mirroring device-tokens.json.
- watch sendTextToPhone: on a transport error, hand the prompt to
  transferUserInfo (OS-durable, FIFO) instead of only persistin

commits.headline: test(a11y): fix Catalyst toggle gate — use targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)
commits.body:
#if os(macOS) is false on Mac Catalyst (iOS-ABI with targetEnvironment),
so the toggle assertion fired on Catalyst builds where HealthSyncSettingsView
renders macHubSection (no toggle). Gate now covers both cases:
  #if os(macOS) || targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)

commits.headline: test(voice): use mic-proven phrases in echo_vocabulary_reuse
commits.body:
Parakeet returns "ember lighthouse" for "amber lighthouse" often enough
that the probe would share a single token with the seeded reply and stop
reproducing the bug. blue triangle / saffron comet are what the other
builtin scenarios already use because they survive the mic path intact.

commits.headline: feat(autojack): flip the judge from Opus to Sonnet 5
commits.body:
Sonnet 5 is near-Opus on this kind of bounded, evidence-bound call at ~1/1.7
the cost, and the judge runs on every routed question. This changes judge
quality characteristics -- that is the point, and it is now measurable rather
than assumed.

commits.headline: feat(autojack): record the concrete judge model on every calibration row
commits.body:
Agreement rate is a property of the judge, not just the decision class.
calibration.js buckets on decisionClass alone, so a window spanning a model
change averages two different judges into one number -- and judge-promotion.js
could promote a class to live on that mixed sample. This adds the column that
makes a pre/post comparison possible at all, and must land before the judge's
model changes.

commits.headline: test(voice): add echo_vocabulary_reuse Tier-2 regression scenario
commits.body:
Probes the 2026-07-25 vanishing-transcript failure: a real user turn that
reuses the assistant's own vocabulary must survive the echo suppressor and
get a reply.

commits.headline: test(a11y): use compile-time guard for healthsync toggle assertion
commits.body:
isDesktopIdiom returns true for iPad too (sidebar probe resolves there),
but on iPad HealthKit is available and iosHealthSection renders the toggle,
so the runtime early-return incorrectly skipped the assertion. Replace with
#if os(macOS) / #else so iPhone and iPad both assert the toggle while
Mac Catalyst (where HealthKit is unavailable) skips it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): stop echo suppressor from deleting real user turns
commits.body:
The realtime CLI was discarding complete, quality-gated final transcripts
as "assistant echo," which dropped the turn AND put the session to sleep —
the user saw their transcript vanish mid-conversation and the agent go
silent. data/voice-transcript.log has 58 of these; replaying the last 12
against their real assistant pairs shows all 12 came through the token
path, none through substring containment.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): keep synthetic traffic out of the replay denominator
commits.body:
The Tier-2 smoke deliberately leaves its telemetry row in `events` — that
row IS the evidence. But judge-routing-replay.mjs reads the same table, so
the synthetic refund question was being counted as real recorded traffic,
landing in both the BEFORE-pages numerator and the denominators of the
harness this branch just made honest about its coverage.

commits.headline: test(autojack): Tier-2 smoke proving human-risk pages are auditable
commits.body:
The unit test for the basePayload fix asserts on an injected telemetryBus, so
it cannot prove what actually lands in the events table — the entire point of
the change. This drives the real router with a real telemetry sink against the
real DB and reads the row back.

fix(bridge): forward native WhatsApp activation metadata
Fix usage contract test: gate on desktop idiom, use XCTSkipUnless for rows

commits.body:
Replace XCTSkipUnless on settings.healthsync.row with XCTAssertTrue —
the Health section is always shown on both iOS and macOS so a skip there
would hide regressions on the iPhone CI target. Replace the silent `if`
branch on settings.toggle.healthSync with a hard XCTAssertTrue, gated
by the existing isDesktopIdiom helper so macOS (where macHubSection
replaces the toggle) exits early without failing.

Follows the mandatory "How to add" step in docs/accessibility-identifiers.md:
testHealthSyncSettingsIdentifiersResolve navigates Settings → Health Sync,
hard-asserts settings.healthsync.syncNow (always present), skips the row
assertion when the Health section is platform-gated off, and conditionally
checks settings.toggle.healthSync only when HealthKit is available
(iOS; absent on macOS which shows the macHubSection instead).

commits.body:
Add the three missing identifiers that complete the Settings → Health Sync
navigation surface: settings.healthsync.row (nav link in SettingsView),
settings.toggle.healthSync (enable toggle), settings.healthsync.syncNow
(upload button). PR #278 covered SettingsView.swift interactive controls

commits.body: Wire up 12 interactive controls in SettingsView that were missing stable automation identifiers per the docs/accessibility-identifiers.md settings.* namespace contract.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): throb the Trial G black hole on a simulated heartbeat
commits.body:
Wires the heart-rate SDK into Trial G so pressing Play produces a visible
pulse with no sensor, no bridge and no fixture.

commits.headline: fix(heart-rate): record verbatim wire frames instead of re-encoded measurements
commits.body:
Integrating the two transports surfaced a real flaw in the SDK seam. The capture
recorder could only observe MeasurementReceived, which is already decoded, so a
"recorded" fixture actually held OUR canonical re-encoding of the strap's data
rather than the strap's own bytes.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): UDP bridge transport and host-side replay tool
commits.body:
Adds the companion-device path: a UDP listener whose datagram payload is a raw
0x2A37 frame. Deliberately dumb and transport-only, so one socket serves the
simulator, a Mac bridge, Home Assistant, or a Pulsoid relay without any further
Unity code.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): direct on-device BLE transport behind a testable seam
commits.body:
Adds the standalone-on-Quest path: the headset connects straight to a BLE Heart
Rate Profile strap over its own Bluetooth radio, no companion phone or PC.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): shared BLE heart-rate SDK with hardware-free simulation
commits.body:
Foundation for driving the black hole pulse from the wearer's real heartbeat.
Verified research established there is no first-party Meta/OpenXR heart-rate or
PPG API on any Quest, and that pupillometry (Quest 3 has no eye tracking; Quest
Pro exposes gaze pose only) and on-headset camera rPPG (passthrough cameras face
outward, away from the wearer) are dead ends. The only real signal is an external
BLE Heart Rate Profile sensor, service 0x180D / characteristic 0x2A37.

commits.headline: fix(runtime): harden incident and voice paths
fix(watch): replace raw Color literals with WatchTheme tokens
commits.body:
Removes the private colorPurple duplicate inside InlineThinkingRibbon
(shadowed WatchTheme.colorPurple) and replaces all remaining raw
Color.orange / Color.yellow / Color.red literals in WatchConversationView
and WatchNowView with their WatchTheme equivalents so the design system
is the single source of truth for watch activity colours.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): tighten AI draft rules and CC-payment heuristic
commits.body:
Require vendor-specific draft match predicates, reject needs_review on
revise/accept, and stop treating bare autopay as a credit-card payment.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): harden AI draft-rule sanitization (Codex P1)
commits.body:

max-spin clamp) instead of a response curve that crushed ordinary

hole can always drift instead of freezing on a hung or non-localizing
scene load. Add once-per-second discriminator logging of load
status/rooms/currentRoom to separate late-completion from
no-relocalization failure modes. The room-load window is deliberately
generous: saved-room relocalization can take many seconds after launch
while head tracking converge

commits.body:
Choose the room collision source deterministically and never combine two
overlapping static sources (which produce duplicate contacts and
depenetration jitter). TrialGRoomColliderPolicy prefers semantic surfaces
whenever the room has both a floor and a wall — cheap synchronous box and
plane colliders — and falls back to the global mesh only for mesh-only
rooms, then a partial semantic set, else nothing (the body stays
kinematic). This flips the previous global-mesh-first behaviour.

commits.body:
Apple's binary validator (ITMS-90683) has rejected every TestFlight upload
since build 10190043 because the com.apple.developer.healthkit entitlement
is present on both the iOS and watch targets, but Info.plist only declared
NSHealthShareUsageDescription. The entitlement itself is unscoped, so Apple
requires the update/write usage string too, even though HealthSyncService
only ever requests read access (toShare: []). PR #263 fixed the sibling
WKBackgroundModes issue from the same rejection email

prs.title: feat(campaigns): PATCH existing broadcasts
prs.body:
## Summary
- Draft campaigns can be updated in place via `PATCH /api/campaigns/:id` (name, subject, preview, markdown, audience).
- Missing IDs return 404. Once a campaign leaves `draft` (`sending` / `sent`), PATCH returns 409 so queue batches keep a stable payload for batch idempotency keys.
- The update is a compare-and-swap (`WHERE status = 'draft'`), so a concurrent send that flips status cannot be overwritten by a later PATCH.

No EOF arrives, the process stays in the event loop, and repeated leaks cause multi-GB swap thrashing.

prs.title: fix(stdio): keep Evernote Thrift errors off MCP stdout
prs.body:
## Summary
- Evernote's `BinaryHttpTransport.log` writes `"Error making Thrift HTTP request…"` to **stdout**, which corrupts the MCP JSON-RPC stream over stdio.
- After one failed Thrift HTTP request, Claude Desktop fails to parse responses (`Unexpected token 'E', "Error maki"...`) and later `get_note` / `search_notes` calls hang until the ~4-minute host timeout.
- Redirect that transport log to stderr via `silenceEvernoteStdio()` before any RPC runs.
